question: A sector of a circle having a radius of 10 cm and has a central angle of (pi)/(6) radians. What is the area of the sector?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for the area of a sector in radians: Area = ½ × r² × θ

Substitute the given values: r = 10 cm and θ = π/6.

Area = ½ × (10)² × (π/6) = ½ × 100 × π/6 = 25π / 3

Using π ≈ 3.14, Area = (25 × 3.14) ÷ 3 = 78.5 ÷ 3 ≈ 26.17 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 26.17 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sector (r) = 10 cm

Central angle (θ) = π/6 radians

**Formula Used:**

Area of a sector = ½ × r² × θ (where θ is in radians)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = ½ × (10)² × (π / 6)

⇒ Area = ½ × 100 × (π / 6)

⇒ Area = 50 × π / 6

⇒ Area = 25π / 3

Using π ≈ 3.14:

⇒ Area = (25 × 3.14) / 3

⇒ Area = 78.5 / 3

⇒ Area = 26.166... ≈ 26.17 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 26.17 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector (in degrees)

If the central angle θ is given in degrees instead of radians, the formula to calculate the area becomes Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Length of an Arc

The length of the arc (s) is calculated directly as s = rθ (if θ is in radians) or s = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr (if θ is in degrees).

Perimeter of a Sector

The total perimeter bounds the sector, including the curved arc length and the two straight radii. It is found using Perimeter = s + 2r.
